The SDK in practice

blocks.title: An API call with an explicit permission

blocks.html:
This request runs through OverCrow and needs a network permission. See the manifest and error states.

Documentation version

JavaScript SDK 1.1.0 · Web API v1 · contract checked against OverCrow 0.5.1-beta.1. Examples use available APIs, not proposed features.

Windows and Linux

OverCrow supports Windows and compatible Linux environments. The creator kit offers the same creation, preview and export workflow on both. The advanced native overcrow-widget dev CLI uses D-Bus on Linux; npm run dev -- --native works on both platforms.

label: Your first widget
title: Your first widget
description: From an empty folder to an installable package, on Windows or Linux.

blocks.html:
1. Download the kit

Install Node.js 22 or later, then download the creator kit and extract it. Open a terminal in overcrow-creator-kit. You need neither the private repository nor Linux tools nor npm install.

You can also start in the online studio and download the finished project or a ready-to-import .ocpkg.

2. Create a counter

blocks.title: Terminal · Windows or Linux
blocks.source:
node overcrow.mjs init my-widget
cd my-widget
npm run dev

blocks.html:
Open the URL printed in the terminal. The counter appears in a page marked as a browser simulation. Click +1 to try it. In PowerShell, use npm.cmd run dev if the execution policy blocks npm.ps1.

3. Change and preview it

Edit the title in widget/index.html, colors in widget/styles.css or button behavior in widget/view.js. The preview reloads valid edits. An invalid edit leaves the last working version visible and explains what to fix.

blocks.title: A regular HTML interaction

blocks.html: 4. Build a package

blocks.title: File hashes are calculated for you
blocks.source:
npm run check
npm run package

blocks.html:
The command prints the .ocpkg path under .overcrow-output/. Only files in widget/ enter the package; tooling and simulated data stay in your project.

5. Test in OverCrow

With OverCrow installed, import the package in Control Center, review its permissions and activate it from the overlay library. Test clicks, resizing and visibility in an actual game session. To replace an installed version, increase version in widget/manifest.json before exporting again. A new file hash alone is not a new version.

Preview versus native runtime

The browser preview helps with layout and simulated scenarios. Clipboard gestures, capture, focus and actual native API behavior need OverCrow. The kit can reload in the native engine on both platforms with --native, but that development session is offscreen. Import a package to test the game overlay.

Where next?

Explore the kit and its fixtures, save preferences, connect an API or add a controller. The checklist template shows persistent state.

label: Installation and compatibility
title: Installation and compatibility
description: Get the SDK and choose a suitable development workflow.

blocks.html:
The easiest starting point

The Windows and Linux creator kit includes the SDK, three templates and local tools. Node.js 22+ is enough to create, preview and export a widget. Follow the quick start or edit online.

Download the SDK separately

Download overcrow.js, TypeScript declarations and the MIT license without an npm registry. The examples include the SDK already.

JavaScript and TypeScript

Write JavaScript directly, or compile TypeScript yourself. Ship the resulting static web files. The .d.ts file supplies types; it does not compile code.

Application and creator tools

CapabilityLinuxWindows
Run an installed widgetSupported on compatible sessionsSupported
Import a local .ocpkgControl CenterControl Center
Create, simulate, check and exportNode.js 22+, npm run dev / check / packageSame kit and commands; no WSL
Native dev, devtools and replayInstalled CLI and same-user Control CenterCompatible OverCrow host; no WSL
Show development session in the game overlayOffscreen; import a package for overlay testingSame behavior
Work on HTML/CSS in a browserYes; native SDK services are simulated or unavailableYes; same limitations

On Linux, use Hyprland 0.55+ Wayland, Plasma 6 Wayland, GNOME 46–50 Wayland or X11/EWMH. On Windows, use Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11 x64 with WebView2 and the application's graphics prerequisites. Windowed and borderless games are supported; exclusive fullscreen is not.

Get OverCrow

Download an official release. On Linux, check that the CLI is installed:

If missing, inspect your installed package. The SDK source package is not currently published to npm; use the files provided here.

Import the SDK

blocks.title: JavaScript module

blocks.html:
Load your file with <script type="module" src="./view.js"></script>. Native services require OverCrow's runtime. A plain browser does not reproduce its network, permissions or input behavior.

View HTML in a browser

Serve the extracted folder with your editor's local server. If Python 3 is installed, you can use:
Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/. Double-clicking index.html may block JavaScript modules on file:// URLs. The kit preview provides a closer host simulation than a plain static server.

label: How a widget works
title: How a widget works
description: A static web project with a view and an optional controller.

headings.title: A controller keeps state through view reloads

blocks.html:
The view draws your interface

The view is a local HTML document. You control components, forms and styles; OverCrow owns the surrounding frame, position, size and panel opacity. Keep the HTML/body background transparent and design for small spaces.

A controller keeps state through view reloads

An optional second HTML document can own caching and requests. It stays alive when a development view is replaced. To survive a full restart, use permitted storage.

Controller · data⇄runtime.send⇄View · interface

A returning view sends a hello message; the controller sends its current state. See a minimal protocol.

Declare capabilities

The manifest names files and permissions for network, game events, storage and clipboard writes. The host enforces them at runtime. Inventing an event name does not create a data source.

Three distinct stages

StageResult
PrepareCopy files, calculate hashes and validate the manifest.
DevelopRegister a temporary folder in the isolated runtime.
DistributeExport a .ocpkg and follow marketplace admission.

Choose a framework

Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript is enough. A framework is fine if it outputs local static files with no Node server or CDN dependency. WASM may be used for local computation. Avoid large bundles and constant background work when hidden.

Ship scripts, styles, images and fonts inside the widget. Remote images, iframes, Web Workers and audio/video media are blocked by the current runtime policy. A manifest network permission allows overcrow.fetch requests; it does not enable those browser facilities.

Explicitly exposed data only

The SDK does not read game memory. Use OverCrow public data or an authorized HTTPS API. Installed widgets run without an AI assistant.

label: Creator kit for Windows and Linux
title: Creator kit for Windows and Linux
description: A project ready to edit, a reloading preview and a package to import into OverCrow.

headings.title: A preview that explains its limits
Simulate an API or game session
Test the same project in OverCrow

blocks.html:
Download the creator kit ↓   Or start in the online studio →

One prerequisite

Install Node.js 22 or later. The kit needs no Rust, WSL, Python, private repository access or npm dependencies. The browser preview is a labeled simulation. To test the game overlay, import an exported package into OverCrow.

Create a project

blocks.title: From the extracted kit folder
blocks.source:
node overcrow.mjs init my-widget --template counter --id com.example.my-widget
cd my-widget
npm run dev

blocks.html:
Choose blank for an empty base (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and manifest), counter for a first example or checklist for persistent state. A controller is optional; Blank has no text to translate. Without --id, the kit generates a distinct ID. It never overwrites an existing folder. Follow the full tutorial.

In the online studio, template selection and reset live in the header. The explorer lets you create, rename, delete and collapse folders and files. After renaming, update imports and file references. Drafts stay in this browser; download the project to keep them elsewhere. Empty folders are preserved in the project ZIP.

Your files

blocks.title: Runtime files are separate from tooling
blocks.source:
my-widget/
  widget/             ← HTML, CSS, JS, manifest and SDK
  preview.json        ← simulation data, not exported
  tooling/            ← local project tools
  package.json        ← development commands
  .overcrow-output/   ← npm run package output

blocks.html:
Keep API keys, personal data and build tools outside widget/. If you use a framework, put its static build output in that folder. The kit does not run your compiler.

Counter and Checklist strings live in widget/locales/en.mjs and widget/locales/fr.mjs. The i18n.mjs helper applies them to HTML elements marked with data-i18n; view.js contains widget interactions. The initial lang="en" default is updated when the SDK supplies the effective locale. Edit a language file to change labels without changing the view.

Everyday commands

CommandResult
npm run dev -- --nativeNative Linux or Windows session; reload the view and retain the controller.
npm run devLocal simulated preview with reload after validation; Ctrl+C stops it.
npm run checkCheck sources and manifest without changing the project.
npm run packageRecalculate hashes and write .ocpkg into .overcrow-output.
npm run doctorReport Node version, OS and available native testing path.

If PowerShell blocks npm.ps1, use npm.cmd run dev or node tooling/overcrow.mjs dev. Do not change your execution policy. Use npm run dev -- --port 4176 for another preview port.

A preview that explains its limits

The terminal prints a 127.0.0.1 URL. Controls simulate an active session, a declared language and active or passive mode. Invalid edits keep the last working view; permission changes require an explicit restart.

The preview includes the required OverCrow frame, font and floating toolbar. Open the three dots to adjust content scale (50–175%) and background opacity (0–100%). Enter a percentage, use the sliders or press Enter. Starter templates open at 100% content scale and background opacity. Content scale reflows within the fixed frame; opacity affects its background and border, not your widget's own CSS background.

Move the widget from its 22-pixel top strip and resize from the lower-right handle, keeping the upper-left corner fixed on the canvas. Focus either control and use arrow keys (Shift for larger steps). Position, frame size and options survive widget reloads until the preview page is refreshed. Escape or an outside click closes the menu.

The frame belongs to OverCrow

Do not recreate the toolbar in widget/. It is never exported. The eye chooses whether the widget stays visible in passive mode. The Mode selector switches the whole overlay, sends overlayMode to the SDK and updates visibility events. SDK widgets keep a manual frame. Passive mode hides the wrapper controls; return to interactive mode to move, resize or adjust the widget. Close remains illustrative. Templates default to English and include French; change their language in the preview.

Reload restarts view and controller. Simulated storage is separated by widget ID and distinct from native storage. Use getItem/setItem, not property syntax such as localStorage.myKey. Test focus, capture and clipboard gestures in OverCrow.

Simulate an API or game session

Declare the corresponding HTTPS permission in the manifest. A fixture matches exact method and URL; request body is not matched. No external request is made. Use text instead of json for text or a status such as 503 to test failure. A missing fixture yields fixture_missing. Arbitrary named game events are not synthesized.

Validate in the native engine

blocks.title: The same commands on Windows and Linux
blocks.source:
npm run dev -- --native
npm run dev -- --native --devtools
npm run dev -- --native --replay ./events.json

blocks.html:
The kit recalculates hashes and hands each valid generation to OverCrow. The controller retains state when the view is replaced. A failure preserves the last accepted generation. Restart after controller code, expanded permissions or storage permission changes; browser storage mode is fixed for a native session. Ctrl+C closes it.

On Linux, use an installed Control Center and overcrow-widget. On Windows, install a compatible host. Portable installations can pass --host "C:/Tools/OverCrow/OverCrow.exe". Node.js is enough; no Rust, WSL or Python is required. npm run doctor reports availability without starting a session.

Offscreen native session

This uses the actual SDK and native engine but does not show the widget over a game. Use the browser preview for layout, devtools for the engine and export/import for the overlay. Older OverCrow versions may need an update.

Test the same project in OverCrow

blocks.title: Same export on Windows and Linux

blocks.html:
Import the printed .ocpkg in Control Center, review permissions and activate the widget. Increase version in widget/manifest.json to replace an installed version; a changed hash alone does not update its version.

Native validation

The kit offers quick feedback. OverCrow and the marketplace remain authoritative for validation and consent. The kit does not sign, install or publish. Native development remains offscreen on both platforms.

Actionable diagnostics

Versioned JSON reports ok, an error code, field and action; failure exits nonzero. Read runtime troubleshooting.

Open Widget Studio ↗

label: The manifest
title: The manifest
description: Declare identity, files and the capabilities your widget needs.

blocks.html: A minimal manifest

The kit adds a files ledger of sizes and SHA-256 hashes to the package; do not maintain it by hand. Keep the widget ID stable across versions because storage and updates use it.

Fields

FieldMeaning
schemaVersion / apiVersionCurrently 1 and the string "1".
idLowercase reverse-domain identifier, for example com.example.my-widget.
versionSemVer such as 1.0.0; increase it for updates.
entrypoints.viewLocal HTML view.
entrypoints.controllerOptional local HTML controller.
permissionsOnly capabilities you actually need.
localizationOptional declared languages and a default locale.
filesGenerated hash/size ledger in the packaged manifest.

A narrow network permission

blocks.title: HTTPS origin, method and path prefix

blocks.html:
A permission does not make arbitrary browser fetches available. Call overcrow.fetch; the runtime checks the exact origin, method and path prefix. Redirects and credentials are restricted. Keep permissions as narrow as possible.

In the online studio, template selection and reset live in the header. The explorer lets you create, rename, delete and collapse folders and files. After renaming, update imports and file references. Drafts stay in this browser; download the project to keep them elsewhere. Empty folders are preserved in the project ZIP.

Prepare trustworthy files

Include local HTML, CSS, JavaScript, fonts and images. Use portable paths and explicit relative references. The creator kit checks duplicate names, unsafe paths, links and native binaries. Only files inside widget/ enter the package; the runtime rechecks the package before installation.

Useful limits

The kit accepts at most 4,096 files and 128 MiB, including the generated manifest. Keep a single manifest, avoid hidden dependencies on a CDN or local server, and include the SDK license with your distributed files. Read widget localization.

label: Examples to build on
title: Examples to build on
description: Three concrete starting points, with sources and permissions.

blocks.html:
Blank · an empty base

Four files: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and manifest, plus the SDK. No sample UI or unnecessary controller. Download sources ↓ or open the studio.

Counter · your first widget

One view, two buttons and a counter. No network or storage. Use it to change a layout, understand the manifest and check packaging. Download counter sources ↓ or edit it online.

Checklist · persistent state

Add, check and remove tasks, then recover them after restart. Local data is versioned and validated; corrupt data is reported without silently overwriting it. Permission: storage: true. Download checklist sources ↓ or edit it online.

Warframe Market · intermediate application

A marketplace example with catalog search, buy/sell offers, IndexedDB cache, separate controller, resynchronized view and message copy. Permissions include GET requests to https://api.warframe.market/v2/, storage and clipboard writes. Download widget sources ↓.

This is reference bundle 2.0.5 from the repository, including its bundled SDK. Downloading it does not create a new publication or catalog entry. Read its source history ↗.

Use the archives

Extract and modify them with the creator kit or Linux native tools. To reuse a source archive in the kit, copy its files into a new project's widget/. Each archive includes the MIT license and its SDK; keep their notices. Choose a distinct ID and suitable version for your own widget.

What the examples prove

The site checks archive files, hashes and script syntax. Rendering and interaction still need native testing on target platforms. Counter and checklist are not published marketplace widgets.

label: Network requests
title: Network requests
description: Use overcrow.fetch for HTTPS requests mediated by the runtime.

headings.title: Read JSON and show a useful error

blocks.html: Signature

blocks.title: JavaScript SDK 1.1.0
blocks.source: overcrow.fetch(url, { method?, headers?, body?, signal? }): Promise<OvercrowResponse>

blocks.html:
Declare an HTTPS origin, method and path prefix in manifest.json. The browser's regular fetch is not a substitute for this permission-checked API. Network requests are bound in size and time by the host; do not rely on redirects or credentials.

Read JSON and show a useful error

blocks.title: Keep the interface usable on failure

blocks.html:
Validate the response schema before displaying it. Never put an API key in a distributed widget. If you need a private key, use a service you control rather than embedding it in the client.

The response

status, ok and contentType describe the result. Use text(), json() or arrayBuffer() once; a second body read raises body_used. A 404 or 503 is an HTTP response, while a denied permission or timeout rejects with an SDK error.

Current constraints

Requests use explicit HTTPS permissions and bounded payloads. A request can be cancelled with an AbortSignal. Fetches through the SDK do not grant remote images, web sockets, workers, cross-origin iframes or browser cookies. Review every declared host and path when publishing.

Stay useful while offline

Show the last validated data when appropriate, distinguish empty results from failed loads, expose a retry action and cancel superseded searches. Look up error codes or study Warframe Market for a larger example.

label: Game session and data
title: Game session and data
description: Read only data that OverCrow explicitly exposes.

blocks.html: Read the current snapshot

blocks.title: Read once

blocks.html:
The snapshot is an explicit runtime contract, not game memory access. Handle missing values and minimal development snapshots.

Current native snapshot fields

FieldMeaning
running / selectedActiveBoolean game/session state; a minimal development snapshot may contain only running.
steamAppIdNumber or null; no title or artwork is implied.
sessionElapsedMsSession duration in milliseconds or null.
overlayMode"passive" or "interactive".
cpuPercentHundredthsProcess CPU percentage in hundredths, or null.
residentBytesResident memory in bytes, or null.
cpuTemperatureMillicelsius / gpuTemperatureMillicelsiusTemperature in thousandths of a Celsius degree, or null.

GameSnapshot types these fields in SDK 1.1.0. Fields may be absent in minimal snapshots; extra JSON fields are kept, but a known field with an invalid type is rejected with invalid_response. Zero is different from missing. The current contract has no FPS, inventory, player health or in-game position field.

Subscribe to native updates

blocks.title: Subscribe, then read the initial state

blocks.html:
onSnapshot delivers subsequent native changes; it does not perform the initial read. Calling the returned unsubscribe function again has no effect. Malformed events are ignored. Continuous polling is unnecessary.

Listen for a named event

Snapshots and demonstration events

game.on receives named events that the host actually delivers or a fixture replays. Native snapshot updates are not automatically session.v1 events. Demonstration fixtures may use elapsedMs, while the native snapshot uses sessionElapsedMs. Use snapshot()/onSnapshot() for current session data.

Test without a game

Replay fixtures exercise declared, ordered events, but cannot simulate every runtime or game capability.

label: View, controller and lifecycle
title: View, controller and lifecycle
description: Exchange state and respond to visibility.

blocks.html: Know the current role

Add "controller": "controller.html" to entrypoints for an optional controller. Both documents import the SDK. Outside OverCrow, the role is unavailable and native calls reject.

A minimal synchronization protocol

blocks.title: Controller keeps in-memory state
View resynchronizes after replacement

blocks.html:
Send plain JSON values: no functions, cycles, Date, Map, undefined or non-finite numbers. A resolved send promise is not proof that business logic handled the message; add a request ID and response if needed. onMessage returns an unsubscribe function.

Visibility

blocks.title: Visibility notification

blocks.html:
Hiding a view need not stop its controller. Keep necessary state work and avoid refresh timers without a reason.

Request a new capture

await overcrow.surface.invalidate() asks the host to refresh a surface. It is not a render engine or animation loop. The runtime already observes page changes; do not call it continuously for a static widget.

label: Storage and persistent state
title: Storage and persistent state
description: Use browser storage in the widget’s private partition.

headings.title: Read a setting with a fallback

blocks.html: Declare persistence

Storage is isolated by widget ID, so preserve that ID through updates. There is no current overcrow.storage API. Use localStorage for small settings and IndexedDB for structured data.

Read a setting with a fallback

blocks.title: Validate data and detect failed saves

blocks.html:
If saving fails, tell the user that changes remain in memory for this session.

A larger cache

Prefer IndexedDB with a versioned schema and transactions whose completion you await. Validate cached data like any external input. Save when state changes; group rapid updates instead of writing on every render.

Protect user work

Show write failures. Do not silently replace invalid content with an empty document. Migrate schemas explicitly and offer recovery. Never put secrets in a distributed package. The checklist demonstrates bounded, versioned local state; Warframe Market shows IndexedDB and a controller.

label: Widget language
title: Widget language
description: Follow the OverCrow preference with translations you provide.

blocks.html: Declare shipped languages

Declare 1–16 unique languages, including the default. Accepted forms include fr, en and en-US. Control Center's preference is matched exactly; otherwise the default is selected.

Read and follow the language

blocks.title: The creator supplies the dictionaries

blocks.html: Without a localization declaration, getCurrent() returns null and no language change is emitted. The host does not translate your widget. Marketplace listing translations are independent of widget text.

label: Copy to clipboard
title: Copy to clipboard
description: An explicit action allowed in interactive mode.

blocks.html: Allow clipboard writes
Copy directly after a click

blocks.title: Text is ready when the user clicks

blocks.html:
Permission alone is insufficient: the current interactive user gesture authorizes one write. Prepare text before the click; waiting for a network response may expire the gesture. Text is limited to 16 KiB and cannot contain NUL.

Report the real result

Wait for success before saying “Copied”. On refusal, leave the action retryable. The SDK cannot read the clipboard.

label: Test and reload
title: Test and reload
description: Reload in the native engine on Windows and Linux, then test in the overlay.

headings.title: The shared Windows and Linux workflow
Replay a fixture without a game

blocks.html: The shared Windows and Linux workflow

The kit validates sources and recalculates hashes. The native view is replaced after loading while the controller stays alive. Restart the session for changed controller code. This session stays offscreen; an imported package is needed to see the widget over a game. Start with the kit and its reloading browser preview.

The advanced Linux loop

Build your framework if necessary, then prepare its static output and register that output with the native CLI. Permissions remain explicit; use a fresh private output directory for each preparation.

blocks.title: Linux · output parent must be private (0700)

blocks.html: Watch a validated folder

The watcher coalesces edit bursts and accepts only consistent manifest and hashes. It keeps the last valid view and its controller when validation fails. It does not compile your framework or recompute hashes; npm run dev -- --native handles those steps for you.

Expanded permissions stop the session with capability_confirmation_required. Review the new manifest and start a fresh registration.

Use a local static server

blocks.title: Server must supply consistent manifest and files

blocks.html:
Use a numeric loopback address and explicit port; localhost is not accepted. The host downloads and freezes verified files. The widget does not connect directly to the server; this is not an HMR or WebSocket tunnel. --watch cannot be combined with --url.

Replay a fixture without a game

Events follow file order, with non-decreasing timestamps. Limits are 1 MiB and 1,024 events. Replay runs again after a successful reload. Here elapsedMs is a fixture field, not the native snapshot's sessionElapsedMs.

Development diagnostics

--devtools opens local developer tools. The terminal reports replacement failures; the inspector shows engine details. Console output can contain private data. Remove tokens and personal responses before sharing a report.

label: Prepare and distribute
title: Prepare and distribute
description: From a local project to a package and marketplace listing.

blocks.html:
Before export

  • Test small sizes, zoom, passive and interactive modes.
  • Handle loading, empty data, failure and recovery.
  • Check saving and returning after the view is hidden.
  • Include every local resource and license in the prepared bundle.

A local package

Run npm run package in a Windows/Linux creator-kit project. The command prints the output path and recalculates hashes. See the complete flow. With the Linux native CLI:

The command validates manifest and files and creates a deterministic stored ZIP with the .ocpkg extension. It neither signs nor installs nor publishes. Changes to bytes require re-preparation, and each new published widget version needs a new version number.

Prepare a listing

listing.json describes the author, license, source and catalog translations. It is separate from runtime files. Listing translations do not declare languages actually supplied by the widget.

Read the marketplace creator guide ↗ and review policy ↗.

Admission and installation

Review and publication use the validated listing, manifest and exact package bytes. The signed catalog and installation consent are separate from local development. “Open in OverCrow” opens a listing in Control Center; it does not install or activate a widget automatically.

Licenses

The SDK and examples here are MIT-licensed; keep their notices. They do not force you to license your own widget under MIT. The public policy for admitting third-party licenses is still pending; successful format validation alone does not authorize publication.

label: Troubleshoot your widget
title: Troubleshoot your widget
description: Find an error, a likely cause and the next concrete step.

headings.title: Isolate the issue in three checks

blocks.html:
Look up an error

Symptom / codeLikely causeNext step
bridge_unavailableThe SDK cannot find the native runtime.Use dev or an installed package; a plain web server has no native bridge.
invalid_manifest / invalid_bundle / invalid widget projectSchema, path, file or hash is inconsistent.Check entrypoints and permissions, then prepare a fresh output.
unsafe_pathRelative path, symlink or incompatible permissions.Use a real absolute path and private 0700 output parent.
capability_confirmation_requiredReload requests more permissions.Review the change and explicitly restart development.
capability_denied / permission_deniedPermission or current user gesture is missing or expired.Check manifest and consent; click again in interactive mode for clipboard.
body_usedThe same response body was read twice.Read json(), text() or arrayBuffer() once and store the result.
invalid_message / message_too_largeMessage is not small, plain JSON.Avoid cycles and split large application data.
request_body_limitRequest body exceeds 2 MiB.Reduce the request or split it if the API permits.
busy / unresponsiveOperation overlaps or runtime did not respond in time.Disable duplicate actions, then offer a retry.
Blank view after an editJavaScript error, missing entrypoint or unprepared build.Open devtools, check index.html and prepare again.
Session events do not fireDeclaring a name does not create a live feed.Use onSnapshot for native SDK 1.1.0 updates; check replay event names/payloads.
HTTP 4xx / 5xxRemote service refused or failed.Check response.ok, show an error and retain last valid data.

Isolate the issue in three checks

  1. Does the HTML render with local assets at the expected size?
  2. Is the widget running in OverCrow with required permissions?
  3. Does received data match the schema your code expects?

Prepare a useful report

Include OverCrow, widget and SDK versions; platform; minimal steps; expected versus actual result; and error code. Use a small example or non-personal fixture. Application diagnostics can prepare a report for explicit submission.

Avoid false leads

The SDK has no shell, Node, Tauri, arbitrary file access or game-memory reading. External browser network access is blocked. An invented manifest permission cannot open those boundaries.
